text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics surprises with profit warning. (p1)
- Maritime services concern Smit Internationale to sell one sixth of its offshore fleet to U.S. Seacor. (p1)
- Retail group Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer (KBB) saw no commercial advantage of a merger with rival Vendex. (p1)
- Transformer maker Smit Trafo finds buyer for its Charleston plant in South Carolina. (p3)
- Postal arm of KPN suffers another setback in its attempt to take over ustralia's TNT. (p3)
- Property developer Bouwfonds in 1:100 share split. (p3)
- Industrial gas producer Hoek Loos takes over U.S. rival Sunox. (p5)
- Transport and storage group Pakhoed takes 51 pct stake in U.S. based Wilmington Liquid Bulk Terminals. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Unions fear 5,000 jobs have to go in new restructuring at Philips Electronics. (p1)
- Industrial sales in July/August up four percent. (p2)
- Spending on innovative research in the Netherlands is rising. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Conflict in insurers association over code of conduct boycott by big insurers. (p25)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm wants to close the door on Britain's participation in European Monetary System. (p7)
- No means yet to stop tax evasion via the Internet. (p29)
- Investment company Robeco's new Click fund draws 512 million guilders from investors.
TROUW
- Aircraft maker Fokker receivers do not mention a buyer yet in their third interim report. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Consumer products giant Unilever to invest an extra $100 million in China. (p13)
- Dispensing chemist's cooperative OPG keeps bandages producer Utermoehlen open. (p13)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
